title: tensorOmics: Data integration for longitudinal omics data using tensor factorisation
abstract: Longitudinal multi-omics studies track molecular changes across biological layers and over time, but repeated measurements from the same subject introduce dependencies that must be accounted for. Conventional matrix-based approaches often flatten the data, obscuring this temporal structure. Tensor methods preserve the multi-way organisation; however, existing approaches are either unsupervised or limited to a single omic, leaving few options for phenotype-guided analysis across multiple longitudinal omics datasets. We present tensorOmics, a framework comprising five tensor methods including an R implementation of TCAM as tensor PCA, spanning exploratory analysis, regression, classification and multi-omics integration. By representing each subject's trajectory in an orthogonal temporal basis, tensorOmics retains subjects as the unit of analysis and enables fitted models to score new subjects. We evaluated the framework using simulations with known temporal signals and in three large public longitudinal cohorts. These evaluations assessed the recovery of group differences encoded in trajectory shape, prediction in held-out subjects and multi-omics integration. Across three biological case studies, our analyses identified relevant temporal patterns and molecular features. Together, these capabilities make tensorOmics a unified framework for analysing longitudinal single- and multi-omic data while preserving their temporal structure.

llm.novelty_zh: 将张量分解（TCAM 作为张量 PCA）与正交时间基相结合，用于纵向多组学的监督式分析与多组学整合，填补了现有张量方法多为无监督或仅限单一组学的空白。
llm.summary_zh: 论文提出 tensorOmics 框架，包含五种张量方法，覆盖纵向单组学与多组学数据的探索性分析、回归、分类和整合。通过将每个受试者的轨迹投影到正交时间基上，模型以受试者为分析单元，并能对新受试者打分。作者在模拟数据和三个大型公开纵向队列上评估了其恢复轨迹形状组间差异、留出受试者预测及多组学整合的能力。
llm.why_it_matters_zh: 该工作针对纵向多组学中重复测量的依赖结构，提供了保留时间维度的张量建模工具，并以 R 实现便于复用。但其主题集中于通用生物信息学数据整合，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型关联较弱。
llm.limitations_zh: 摘要未提及具体数据集名称、与主流多组学整合方法的定量对比结果，也未涉及单细胞或扰动场景。

title: DemuxHMM: Large-Scale Single-Cell Embryo Profiling via Recombination Barcoding
abstract: High-resolution developmental time-courses with single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) increasingly target trajectory inference and other analyses in the study of development and disease. Researchers can efficiently generate these datasets by pooling individuals and inferring cell-to-individual mappings after sequencing, in a process called demultiplexing. Existing demultiplexing methods face limitations in the number of timepoints they can support, due to either the need for individual-by-individual processing or reduced accuracy at large numbers of individuals. To address these limitations, we introduce a computational framework for demultiplexing large-scale, individual-resolved datasets. Our framework includes a recombination-aware demultiplexing method, DemuxHMM, which uses a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) to explicitly model contiguous SNP patterns that arise from simple breeding schemes. We demonstrate substantial performance and scalability gains from this recombination-aware approach on both a real Diversity Outbred (DO) mouse data and a simulated Drosophila dataset. This performance demonstrates the value of the method when used for common applications on model organisms such as time series, crossover position inference, and eQTLS, among others.

llm.novelty_zh: 用基于HMM的重组感知（recombination-aware）SNP模式建模来做大规模多个体混池scRNA-seq的去复用（demultiplexing），可扩展到更多时间点。
llm.summary_zh: 该文提出 DemuxHMM，用隐马尔可夫模型显式建模由简单育种方案产生的连续 SNP 模式，用于对混池 scRNA-seq 中的细胞进行个体归属（demultiplexing）。方法在 Diversity Outbred 小鼠真实数据和模拟果蝇数据上展示了性能与可扩展性提升，并可用于时间序列、交换位置推断和 eQTL 等分析。该工作属于单细胞数据预处理与实验设计工具，与虚拟细胞、扰动建模或细胞基础模型关系较弱。
